arguments.summary: Commodities role finds no independent, evidenced commodity-price signal for the 63-session comparison. The usable evidence supports product-demand/pricing and customer-infrastructure channels, but does not quantify energy, metals, wafer/material contract pricing, or pass-through sensitivity; memory pricing should not be treated as a quoted commodity series.

claims.text: Micron’s Q3 FY2026 release reported sharply higher revenue and gross margin and guided Q4 GAAP gross margin to about 86%; it also identified AI-memory products and volume shipments. This establishes product pricing/mix and demand as operating variables, not an oil/metals exposure.

NVIDIA guided Q3 FY2027 revenue and gross margin while stating no assumed China Data Center compute revenue, and disclosed land, power and shell guarantees for select AI-cloud partners. Power availability is therefore a potential indirect customer buildout constraint, rather than a disclosed NVIDIA energy-input-cost sensitivity.

For MU, a change in memory product pricing/mix or customer demand could move revenue and gross margin before any unobserved raw-material cost effect; for NVDA, a delay in customer data-center power/site readiness could defer system demand, partly offset by continued platform deployment. Neither mechanism can be sized from supplied evidence.

QQQ’s dated September 18 holdings include NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%. This establishes look-through overlap with the two issuers, but does not establish QQQ commodity beta or the fund’s exposure to their unquantified input costs.

gaps.description: The supplied filings/results do not provide a quantified energy, metals, substrates/wafer-material cost exposure, contract pricing, hedging, pass-through, or relevant commodity-price series for NVDA or MU. The filings were inspected for materials/inventory, but inventory balances do not identify input-price sensitivity. Consequently this role cannot quantify a commodity-driven margin impact or rank NVDA, MU and QQQ on commodity risk.

assumptions: Product pricing means issuer semiconductor/memory selling price and mix, not a quoted commodity benchmark.
Any power constraint acts through AI-cloud/customer capacity and timing; it is not assumed to be an NVIDIA electricity input-cost exposure.
QQQ weights are dated sponsor holdings, not current holdings or a personalized portfolio exposure.
arguments.counter_thesis: Material and energy inputs can matter substantially in semiconductor fabrication, while data-center power availability may constrain AI deployments. That alternative remains plausible, but no supplied disclosure quantifies the affected operating line, contractual mitigation, or timing, so it cannot support an independent directional assessment.

review_conditions.description: Review after the next MU results/filing if it discloses a material change in DRAM/NAND pricing, inventory, raw-material/wafer costs, energy costs, or supply commitments. A disclosed margin bridge would determine whether the assumed Q4 demand/margin cases need a cost-pressure or price-realization adjustment.

Review after NVIDIA’s next results/filing if disclosed customer power/site delays, guarantees, supply-component constraints, or data-center deployment timing change. Evidence of delayed deployments would weaken the demand-timing premise; evidence of completion or additional committed capacity would strengthen it.

shared_exposures.mechanism: QQQ has dated holdings in both issuers, so any issuer-specific product-pricing or customer-capacity development can transmit indirectly to the fund; this is overlap only, not evidence of commodity beta, and omitted holdings/cash/derivatives limit full look-through.
shared_exposures.qualification: Weights are dated September 18, 2026 sponsor data; neither issuer’s commodity-cost sensitivity is quantified in the supplied evidence.
